name: web
//overrides: 12 high-severity advisories, both packages reached only through next, which pins postcss to an
exact 8.4.31 and takes sharp as an optional ^0.34.5. So `npm audit fix` cannot touch either and
`npm audit fix --force` proposes next@9.3.3 — a 2020 release — to fix 2026 advisories. Downgrading
seven major versions to silence an audit trades a real vulnerability for a much larger one.
Overrides move them forward instead. Both are patch/minor bumps within the same major, and the
build + typecheck + 15-route render is what proves the pin still holds.
ponytail: an override is a claim that next works with a version it did not pick. Revisit on every
next upgrade — if it starts declaring postcss >=8.5.18 and sharp >=0.35 itself, delete this block
rather than leaving a pin that silently holds a dependency back.
NOT overridden, deliberately: brace-expansion (GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, DoS via unbounded expansion).
It is the single root behind the 9 advisories that remain, reached only through minimatch under
eslint and its plugins. `"brace-expansion": "^5.0.8"` does take the audit to 0 — and breaks the
linter: 5.x changed its export shape, minimatch@3.1.5 calls it as `expand()`, and every eslint run
then dies with `TypeError: expand is not a function`. A clean audit and a dead lint is a worse
trade than a build-time DoS advisory, so the number stays at 9 with a reason.
It also does not reach production: the Dockerfile is multi-stage and the runtime image copies only
.next/standalone + .next/static, so /app/node_modules holds 10 packages and no eslint. Verified by
searching the built image, not inferred from the Dockerfile. Clears when eslint's plugins move to
minimatch >=10; re-run `npm audit` after any eslint bump and drop this note if it reports 0.
